name: Can Tho food
summary: Can Tho eats from the Cái Răng boats at dawn, from Đề Thám in town, and from the garden tables at Mỹ Khánh. Hủ tiếu on the water is the bowl the Mekong towns page treats as this city’s breakfast.
body: The morning is a bowl passed across the gunwale: hủ tiếu, bún riêu, cà phê vợt, and bún chả cá, while the wholesale boats trade. Vietnam Tourism’s place page then names a Can Tho crispy pancake, lẩu mắm, cá lóc nướng, a fried shrimp cake, and canh chua. The four-day piece puts nem nướng Cái Răng at lunch and a second canh chua at dinner in town.

Đề Thám is the street Vietnam Tourism calls a primer for southern cooking. Bún nước lèo is served there and at Mỹ Khánh, and the dining page says the noodle hails from Soc Trang, 60 km southeast. Cá tai tượng and bông bí chiên giòn are Mekong plates in the chapter that uses Can Tho as a base, not dishes the chapter says were born here. Châu Đốc is the other base in that chapter. Stall prices were not printed. Check on arrival.
specialtiesLead: Hủ tiếu, bánh xèo, and canh chua are the plates with a photograph. The other names follow as text, with the area the account gives.

sections.heading: Can Tho plates
paragraphs: These are the other plates Vietnam Tourism and the Can Tho tourism department tie to the city, the quay, Cồn Sơn, or Mỹ Khánh. A shop hour that was not printed is Check on arrival. Fried shrimp cake has no Vietnamese name on the place page. Bánh cống is a separate fritter.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These plates are eaten in Can Tho and belong to a wider Mekong account. Cá tai tượng and bông bí chiên giòn are not given a Can Tho birthplace. Bún nước lèo hails from Soc Trang on the dining page, is served on Đề Thám and at Mỹ Khánh, and is eaten in Tra Vinh on the four-day piece.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: The everyday places are the boats, Đề Thám, the night market, chợ cổ, the Mỹ Khánh tables, and the quay snack row. A named dining room is not a pick.

spots.name: Cai Rang boats
spots.note: Breakfast on the water while the wholesale boats trade: hủ tiếu, bún riêu, cà phê vợt, and bún chả cá. The department and Vietnam Tourism print several morning clocks. A boat fare on the department listing is đang cập nhật. The department advice page prints 300,000–700,000 VND a boat.

spots.name: De Tham
spots.note: Vietnam Tourism says Đề Thám is known locally as food street, a primer for southern cooking, and that the move is to sit where it is busy. An hour was not printed. Check on arrival. A street number for the whole row was not printed.

spots.name: Ninh Kieu night market
spots.address: Đường Hai Bà Trưng, phường Ninh Kiều
spots.note: The department listing says fruit, clothes, jewelry, handicrafts, and seafood, on a paved lane, with stalls setting up around 16:00. Hours on the listing: 17:00–22:00. The 2016 portal’s quay snacks are about 16:00–19:00 and may be the same crowd or a different row. A footer line of 98 Phan Đình Phùng is not the market address on this evidence.

spots.name: Can Tho old market
spots.address: Hai Bà Trưng, phường Ninh Kiều
spots.note: The quay page puts chợ cổ on the Ninh Kiều walk with Chùa Ông. A department tour text says the hall is on Hai Bà Trưng and that a first building dates from around 1915. Daytime hours: Check on arrival.

spots.name: My Khanh garden tables
spots.address: 335 Lộ Vòng Cung, about 10 km from the centre
spots.note: Eat the garden plates after the fruit, at midday on the 2016 portal. A department tour text says more than 30 ha. A one-day article says more than 50,000 m². Newer lines say phường An Bình. Older lines say xã Mỹ Khánh, huyện Phong Điền. A fee: Check on arrival.

spots.name: Quay snack row
spots.address: The road to Bến Ninh Kiều
spots.note: The Can Tho Portal of 4 January 2016 says that from about 16:00 the quay stalls sell xôi bắp, xôi đậu phộng, xôi trắng, barbecue, bánh xèo, bread, and sweet potato, until about 19:00. Eat on the spot or on a bench in the park.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Dawn on the Cái Răng boats is bún riêu, cà phê vợt, and bún chả cá, with hủ tiếu above. The clocks for the market do not agree. Be on the water in the morning.

seoTitle: Can Tho food: boats, De Tham, My Khanh
seoDescription: Hủ tiếu at Cái Răng, bánh xèo, canh chua, Đề Thám, and the Mỹ Khánh garden plates. Soc Trang’s bún nước lèo is served here and is not a Can Tho invention.
